### Position read
Opening position. We moved Red from (0,3) to the central square (3,3), creating a center foothold with no capture. All colors remain intact at 0 losses.
### Our plan
Use Red and Yellow to claim complementary central squares while preserving clear files. Exploit same-color sandwich tactics around the Red anchor: an opponent landing adjacent on row 3 may be captured by a second Red arriving beyond it. Watch for a fast four-center win, but do not let our pieces block each other’s routes.
### Opponent tendencies
No opponent move observed yet.
### Lessons
Only identical colors form sandwich endpoints; our two colors cooperate for center control but not captures. Recalculate captures only around each landing square, including friendly fire and enclosure.

### Position read
We hold centers (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; Blue occupies (3,4). All colors have 0 losses. Green acts next. Our Yellow on (4,3) blocks Green from reaching (4,4) horizontally from the left edge.
### Our plan
On the next Red turn, if still legal, move Red (0,5) to (3,5): the landing Red and Red at (3,3) sandwich and capture Blue at (3,4). Then pursue the vacated central squares (3,4) and (4,4) for a rapid center win while keeping routes open.
### Opponent tendencies
Blue immediately contested our first center by moving from (3,7) to (3,4), but entered a one-move Red sandwich.
### Lessons
Before every move, inspect same-color far flanks in all four directions. Central occupation can constrain edge pieces’ rook paths even without captures.

### Position read
Red moved (0,5) to (3,5), sandwiching Blue at (3,4) against Red at (3,3). Blue now has 1 loss. We retain Red at (3,3) and Yellow at (4,3); central squares (3,4) and (4,4) are empty. Green at (5,4) blocks Yellow’s direct vertical route from (7,4).
### Our plan
Defend our two center occupants and work toward filling (3,4) and (4,4). On Yellow’s next turn, assess whether (4,4) can be occupied safely without vacating (4,3); otherwise develop another Yellow toward row 4. Watch for immediate enemy entry into the cleared (3,4).
### Opponent tendencies
Blue contested the center directly and overlooked a same-color sandwich flank. Green developed from the edge to (5,4), incidentally blocking a direct Yellow central route.
### Lessons
Exploit same-color far flanks immediately. For center victory, avoid moving an existing central piece merely to shift between center squares unless its vacated square can be refilled at once.

### Position read
Yellow shifted from (4,3) to (4,4), denying Green’s immediate move from (5,4) into that center square. We now hold Red at (3,3) and Yellow at (4,4); (3,4) and (4,3) are empty. Red can likely reach (3,4) from (0,4). Green may enter (4,3) from (4,0), but that would be vulnerable to a future Yellow landing at (4,2), using Yellow at (4,4) as the far flank.
### Our plan
On Red’s turn, prioritize occupying (3,4) if still legal and tactically safe. Preserve Yellow at (4,4). If Green takes (4,3), consider Yellow (7,2) to (4,2) to capture it. Otherwise develop that Yellow toward (4,2), then seek to fill (4,3) for center victory.
### Opponent tendencies
Blue contests central lanes; Green’s piece at (5,4) creates immediate center pressure. The opponent may use the vacated (4,3) to interrupt our center formation.
### Lessons
Occupy threatened center squares before slow development. A center intruder can be bait if two same-color flanks can be formed by the next landing move.

### Position read
We hold Red at (3,3) and (3,4), plus Yellow at (4,4); only (4,3) remains for center victory. Green at (4,0) currently has a line toward (4,3), while Green at (2,3) is blocked from descending by Red at (3,3). Blue at (4,5) is blocked from moving left by Yellow at (4,4).

### Our plan
On Yellow’s next turn, if safe and legal, move Yellow (7,2) to (4,2). This blocks Green’s horizontal route into (4,3) and prepares Yellow (4,2) to step into (4,3) on its following turn for an immediate center win. Preserve all three current center occupants. Reassess any Blue move that attacks the setup or occupies column 2.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has developed Green toward central lanes and may now seek a blocking move, capture threat, or obstruction on (4,2). Blue is likely the immediate defensive resource because Green acts only after our Yellow turn.

### Lessons
With three center squares secured, prioritize sealing access to the fourth and staging an aligned piece to enter it. Check intervening blockers carefully: occupied center pieces can protect against rook-like intrusion.

### Position read
We occupy three center squares: Red at (3,3) and (3,4), Yellow at (4,4). Yellow is now staged at (4,2), so (4,3) is the sole missing center square. This staging piece also blocks Green at (4,0) from reaching the target. Green at (2,3) cannot descend through Red (3,3), and Blue at (4,5) cannot cross Yellow (4,4).

### Our plan
Preserve the three center occupants and Yellow (4,2). On Yellow’s next turn, move (4,2) to (4,3) for immediate center victory if still legal. On the intervening Red turn, prioritize preventing any Blue disruption or occupation of (4,3); avoid moving a center Red unless forced.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is developing toward central lanes and has used Blue to capture near the center. Green now has the first defensive chance, followed by Blue after our Red turn, so inspect both moves for captures, blockers, or attacks on the staged Yellow.

### Lessons
A one-square staging move can both deny the opponent’s rook lane and create an unavoidable center-entry threat. Recheck captures around every landing square before executing the final occupation.

### Position read
We retain Red at (3,3) and (3,4), Yellow at (4,4), and staged Yellow at (4,2). The sole missing center square is (4,3). Green’s move to (5,3) did not attack or block the winning entry. After the quiet Red move to (1,1), Blue has no direct rook path to (4,3) and no immediate sandwich against a center occupant.

### Our plan
If Blue does not alter the center situation, play Yellow (4,2) to (4,3) for immediate center occupation victory. Before doing so, verify the destination remains empty, the path is clear, and all three existing center pieces remain ours.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has centralized Green at (2,3) and (5,3), while Blue holds (4,5), but our center pieces interrupt their critical lanes. Expect Blue’s final defensive attempt to target a center occupant or manufacture a blocker.

### Lessons
When a center win is one tempo away, use the intervening color’s move harmlessly and preserve every required occupant and access lane.

### Position read
Yellow’s move from (4,2) to (4,3) completes the center alongside Red at (3,3) and (3,4) and Yellow at (4,4).

### Our plan
Center occupation is complete, so we win immediately.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent’s last Blue move to (5,4) did not disrupt our center or block Yellow’s winning path.

### Lessons
Preserving the staged one-step center entry through the intervening turns converted the positional advantage into an immediate win.
